service-lib.description: Not a value: Helm puts a key named for every sub-chart into the values it validates.

title: web chart values
description: Two blocks and the image map: `platform` is the platform schema, `config` is the service's own schema, and the chart adds nothing between them.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: platform
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: What the platform provides one component of a service chart: the image, the replicas, the account it runs as, how it is probed, where its identity is mounted, which secrets reach it as environment variables, and how it exports telemetry. The shape of the `platform` block of a chart's values, read by the library chart (decision 0009). Nothing here is the service's own configuration: that is the chart's `config` block, which is the service's schema and nothing else.

image.description: Where the image is. A digest when there is one; a tag only when there is not. Left out, the library reads the chart's own top-level `images.<component>`, the map a release stamps and refuses to publish with an empty digest.

replicas.description: Defaults to 1. A service that must survive a rollout runs more than one: one instance cannot be replaced without a gap whatever the strategy says.

strategy.description: The rolling update. The defaults make a rollout gapless: the replacement is READY before the incumbent is touched.

resources.description: Kubernetes' own resource requirements. Open: it is passed through unchanged.

podSecurity.description: Who the process is. Every field defaults to 65532, the unprivileged user the runtime images run as; `fsGroup` is the one that matters, because a CSI driver writes what it mounts owned by root.

create.description: False where the platform creates the accounts; they must then exist. Defaults to true.

serviceAccount.description: The account this component runs as. EVERY component has its own, always; `default` is refused. The library grants nothing: annotations are where a platform binds the account to rights outside the cluster, and which mechanism does that is the platform's.

enabled.description: Defaults to whether `config.listen` exists. Enabling one for a component that listens on nothing is refused.

service.description: A component that listens has a Service on the ports of its own `config.listen`; one that does not has none.

startup.description: Absent means no startup probe. Present, it needs at least one field.

probes.description: How the component is probed, on the listener its own `config.probes` binds. Liveness is nothing but the process: a probe that checks a dependency restarts a healthy process and makes an outage worse.

preStopSeconds.description: Fail readiness, then wait this long before the drain starts, so that whatever routes traffic has removed this endpoint first. Defaults to 5.

drain.description: The service's own shutdown budget is `config.drain.seconds`; the library derives the grace period from it and this delay, so the three numbers cannot disagree.

csiDriver.description: The driver that mounts the identity. The platform's, so there is no default; required once the identity is mounted.

mount.description: Defaults to whether `config.tls.mode` is permissive or strict. True mounts the identity into a component that presents none of its own, because the release does; false never mounts it.

tls.description: Where the platform mounts the workload identity. The files the component's own `config.tls` names must be under `mountPath`; the render refuses a file that is not.

telemetry.description: OpenTelemetry's own environment variables (decision 0006): they leave the chart as variables, never as configuration keys. No endpoint means do not export.

secrets.description: The environment variables that carry SECRETS, and nothing else (decision 0002): variable name to the Secret and key its value comes from. The configuration file names the VARIABLE; the value never appears in a values file or a render.

env.description: Environment a platform CLIENT LIBRARY reads (a database client's connection variables, for example), never the service's own configuration: a service takes no other structural input than its file (decision 0002). A secret does not belong here; declare it in `secrets`.

volumes.description: Extra pod volumes, in Kubernetes' own shape, for what a client library mounts (a trust bundle, a password file). Open: passed through unchanged.

volumeMounts.description: The mounts for `volumes`, in Kubernetes' own shape.

mountPath.description: The directory the ConfigMap is mounted at. Defaults to `/etc/<chart name>`.

pathFlag.description: The argument that carries the path. Defaults to `-config`.

pathEnv.description: When set, the path is passed in this environment variable instead of an argument.

config.description: How the file reaches the process. The path is ONE argument or ONE environment variable, never both (decision 0002).

annotations.description: For a ConfigMap that must be a hook resource: a pre-install job cannot mount one the release has not created yet.

https://example.com/url-shortener/schema.title: web
https://example.com/url-shortener/schema.description: The front end: serve the page, and ask the service that owns the tables. It writes nothing and holds no database credential.

urls.description: The service that owns the URL tables. An address and nothing else: which protocol the caller speaks is in its code, and whether the connection is authenticated is the tls block's business.

mode.description: `report-only` sends Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: a browser reports a violation to its console (and to reportUri) and blocks nothing. `enforce` sends Content-Security-Policy. `off` sends neither.

connectSrc.description: Origins the page may connect to besides its own, added to `connect-src 'self'`. Each is a bare origin, scheme and host and optional port, never a path and never a keyword.

reportUri.description: Where a browser POSTs violation reports. A path on this origin or an absolute URL; empty or absent adds no report-uri directive.

csp.description: The Content-Security-Policy this server sends with every response. Absent means report-only with no extra origins: the header is sent, nothing is blocked, so turning it on cannot break a page.

collectorUrl.description: Where the page POSTs telemetry: a path on its own origin (the default, `/faro/collect`, which the gateway routes to the collector, so connect-src 'self' is enough) or an absolute HTTPS URL, whose origin is then added to connect-src.

apiKey.description: The app's public key at the collector, sent as `x-api-key`. A public identifier, not a secret.

appName.description: The app name the collector sees.

environment.description: A label for where this install runs, for example `devel`.

sampleRate.description: The fraction of browser SESSIONS that report anything, 0 to 1.

faro.description: Browser telemetry (Grafana Faro). Absent, or `enabled: false`, means the page sends nothing and the Faro libraries are never downloaded. Every field here is written into the page for every visitor to read: `apiKey` is a PUBLIC identifier of this app at the collector (one key per app, rotatable, paired with the collector's origin allow-list), not a secret, and no credential may be put in this block.

assets.description: Where the built page is. A path rather than an embedded bundle, because the assets are the one thing in this image that a CDN might serve instead.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: listen
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: A TCP listener. `address` is a host:port the service binds; an empty host binds every interface.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: tls
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: Mutually authenticated transport, where the platform provides the identity. A workload presents a certificate it did not mint, reloads it without restarting, and admits peers by the account they run as rather than by the address they call from. Absent, or mode 'off', means cleartext: a service must be installable on a platform that provides none of this.

mode.description: 'off' serves cleartext only. 'permissive' serves BOTH, on two ports, so that an edge can migrate one side at a time without a coordinated window. 'strict' serves only the authenticated port. One listener cannot be both in every runtime, which is why permissive is two ports rather than one that sniffs.

address.description: Where the authenticated listener binds under 'permissive', beside the cleartext one. Under 'strict' there is one listener and it is the service's own, so this is unused: the protocol changes, the address does not, and nothing downstream has to be told.

certFile.description: The certificate this workload presents, mounted and rotated by the platform. Re-read when it changes, never cached for the process's lifetime: a one-hour certificate outlives no deployment.

keyFile.description: Its private key. It lives in the pod and never in a secret, so a workload that can read secrets in its namespace still cannot read a neighbour's key.

caFile.description: The authority peers are verified against, distributed by the platform as a trust bundle.

trustDomain.description: The root of every identity this service will admit, for example 'example.internal'. A peer whose identity belongs to another trust domain is refused before its account is even considered.

peers.description: Who may call. Each entry is an ACCOUNT, not an address: an address resolves to whoever holds it today. An empty list admits no one, which is the correct default for a service nobody has been granted.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: service
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: The envelope every service's configuration carries. A service references this from its own schema with allOf, and adds its own properties beside it. What is in here is what EVERY component has, including a job that exits and a consumer that answers nothing: somewhere to report health, a log level, and a shutdown budget. A listener is not one of those — see docs/contracts/config.md.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: probes
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: The health listener. Separate from the service's own traffic, so that readiness is answerable when the service's listener is saturated, and so that a probe is not reachable from outside.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: log
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: Structured logging. One level for the whole service: per-package levels are deliberately not part of the contract.

level.description: The lowest level that is written.

https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.title: drain
https://github.com/truvity/policy/schema.description: How long the service may take to finish in-flight work after SIGTERM. It is one number shared with whatever deploys the service: the grace period granted to the process and the pre-stop delay before it are derived from this, so that a draining process is never killed at the moment it would have finished.

seconds.description: Seconds to finish in-flight work. Unset means the service's own default, which is only correct if nothing external is counting.
